check.title: Where are you right now, and what do you feel?
check.hint: A short HALT check. There are no right or wrong answers.

items.label: Tired / unrested
items.tip: Urges get stronger when you're tired. Going to bed a little earlier tonight could help.

items.label: Hungry
items.tip: Hunger increases tension. Eating something or drinking water calms your body.

items.label: Lonely
items.tip: Loneliness is one of the most common triggers. Messaging someone or going somewhere with people around can help.

items.label: Angry / stressed
items.tip: Tension looks for a way out. Breathing or a short burst of movement can ease that load.

check.intensity: How strong is the urge right now?

relocate.title: Action first
relocate.lead: You don't need to fight the urge. Just get up from where you are right now.
relocate.done: You changed place. This small step puts distance between the urge and the behaviour.

tools.title: Choose a tool
tools.hint: Try as many as you like. When you finish one you can move on to another.

items.title: What you can do
items.desc: 8 steps you can take right now

breath.desc: Quick calm: take two short breaths in and one long breath out. In studies, a few minutes of slow breathing had positive effects on reducing stress.

puzzle.desc: Place the pieces on the board and full rows disappear. In studies, a visual puzzle that keeps your mind busy reduced the strength of urges.
puzzle.srHint: This puzzle is played by looking at the screen. With a screen reader on, we suggest the breathing tool.

move.desc: A short burst of movement redirects your energy. Each move is 30 seconds; go at your own pace.
move.done: You've finished the set. Your body may feel different right now.

values.desc: You wrote down yourself what kind of person you want to be in this:
values.empty: You haven't chosen a value yet. You can add one from the panel.

futureSelf.desc: Write yourself a letter to read in a hard moment. Remind yourself what you feel and why you're on this path.
futureSelf.placeholder: Dear me, if you're reading this…
futureSelf.saved: Your letter has been saved, encrypted.

supporter.desc: Write to someone you trust. The message is neutral; it contains no details.
supporter.message: I'm going through a hard moment right now, can we talk?

end.question: How are you now?
end.managedBody: The urge came and you chose to watch it. Every moment you manage makes the next one a little easier.
end.hardBody: That's okay; some waves last longer. Let's try another tool: {tool}.
end.slippedTitle: This is part of the journey
end.slippedBody: Being hard on yourself doesn't make the next time easier. A slip doesn't mean all your effort is erased. If you like, let's log what happened.
end.count: So far you've managed {n} urge moments.

emergency: In an emergency, call 112 (or your local emergency number).

actions.title: What you can do
actions.lead: An urge is like a wave: it rises, peaks and usually fades within 15–20 minutes. Do one or more of these now and tick what you did.

items.title: Change your surroundings
items.text: Leave the room you're in; turn on the light or go where there are people.

items.title: Put the phone away
items.text: Leave the phone in another room, or turn the screen off and face it down.

items.title: Cold water
items.text: Wash your face with cold water or slowly drink a glass of water.

items.title: A short walk
items.text: Go outside or walk briskly around the house for 5–10 minutes.

items.title: Keep your hands busy
items.text: Find a small hands-on job: the dishes, tidying up, fixing something.

items.title: Take a shower
items.text: A warm or cool shower resets body and mind.

items.title: Move on to your next task
items.text: Pick something on your plan and do its first 2 minutes right away.

items.title: Decide in 15 minutes
items.text: Tell yourself "not now, I'll decide in 15 minutes"; the urge usually passes in that time.

actions.note: These are steps anyone can take anywhere. If urges are frequent and hard, getting support from a professional is a strong step.
